$comment: PLAIN-LANGUAGE CATEGORY FACTS. Step 3 of the GEO guide: state what a treatment category is, who it is for and what it addresses, in fact-dense sentences placed before any marketing copy. `addresses` is the inverse of CONCERN_CATEGORIES in src/content/brand.ts — keep the two in step. Nothing here makes a clinical or outcome claim, and every category ends at the consultation, matching the wording Nurella supplied.

laser.whatItIs: Laser treatments use focused light energy, delivered by a device, to work on hair growth or the surface and deeper layers of the skin. The lounge's laser menu covers laser hair removal, CO2 laser, HIFU and RF microneedling.
laser.whoItIsFor: People looking for longer-term hair reduction, or for skin-surface and firmness work that a topical facial cannot reach.

skin-care.whatItIs: Professional facial treatments performed in the lounge — deep cleansing, HydraFacial, diamond technique, meso lifting and microneedling — focused on cleansing, hydration and the condition of the skin's surface.
skin-care.whoItIsFor: Anyone maintaining their skin, preparing it before an event, or dealing with congestion, dullness or rough texture.

permanent-makeup.whatItIs: Semi-permanent cosmetic tattooing of the brows, lips and eyeline — microblading, nano blading, lip blush and eyeliner — designed to follow your natural features.
permanent-makeup.whoItIsFor: People who want their brows, lips or eyeline defined without applying makeup daily, including anyone with sparse or uneven brows.

nails.whatItIs: Nail care and finishing: manicure, pedicure, gel polish and gel extensions.
nails.whoItIsFor: Clients booking routine nail maintenance or a longer-lasting finish for an occasion.

facial-aesthetics.whatItIs: Non-surgical facial treatments that work on proportion and definition — facial contouring, lip and cheek enhancement, chin and jawline contouring, face sculpting, Botox, face slimming and under-eye rejuvenation.
facial-aesthetics.whoItIsFor: People who want to refine facial balance, restore definition or soften expression lines without surgery.

collagen-biostimulation.whatItIs: Treatments designed to support the skin's own collagen production over a series of sessions — PLLA collagen stimulation, CaHA biostimulation and personalized collagen-stimulator protocols.
collagen-biostimulation.whoItIsFor: People noticing loss of firmness or structure who prefer a gradual, progressive change rather than an immediate one.

skin-boosters-rejuvenation.whatItIs: Injectable and regenerative skin-quality treatments — skin boosters, polynucleotides, mesotherapy, exosome therapy, glow and brightening protocols and anti-aging protocols — aimed at hydration, radiance, elasticity and texture rather than volume.
skin-boosters-rejuvenation.whoItIsFor: People whose main concern is skin quality: dryness, dullness, fine crepiness or tired-looking skin.

advanced-skin-treatments.whatItIs: Device- and technique-led treatments for the skin's structure and surface, including HIFU, microneedling protocols and resurfacing approaches selected during the consultation.
advanced-skin-treatments.whoItIsFor: People with established concerns — acne marks, pigmentation, enlarged pores or uneven texture — that routine facials have not resolved.

lifting-contouring.whatItIs: Non-surgical lifting and contouring treatments that work on facial firmness and definition along the cheeks, jawline and neck.
lifting-contouring.whoItIsFor: People seeing sagging or a softening jawline who are not looking for surgery.

beauty-nails.whatItIs: Beauty and nail services grouped together for clients combining a beauty appointment with nail care.
beauty-nails.whoItIsFor: Clients booking beauty and nail services in the same visit.
